caption: Italy officially bans gender-neutral symbols in schools.
Italy’s Education Ministry has instructed schools to stop using gender-neutral symbols such as the asterisk (*) and the schwa (ə) in official communication.
Officials said these symbols are not consistent with Italian grammar and could make language less clear and harder to understand.
The move is part of a broader cultural debate, as the government—led by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni—has emphasized traditional language and values.
Supporters argue the decision protects linguistic clarity, while critics say it limits inclusive language and could affect non-binary representation in schools.
The policy has sparked reactions across the country, highlighting ongoing tensions around language, identity, and education.
